beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: To multiply by ten, I add a zero. Thirty-six becomes three hundred sixty.

do.text: Does adding a zero always work?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try three point six times ten.

do.text: Does adding a zero always work?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Three point six zero?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That is still three point six. Zero hundredths adds nothing. The three and six have not changed places.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So what does multiplying by ten really change?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A place tells what a digit is worth. Here is one whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Cut it into ten equal parts. Each part is one tenth.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten tenths make one whole. Ten ones make one ten. Each place is worth ten times the place just to its right.

do.text: Each step left: ten times as much.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So six tenths, made ten times as much, becomes six ones.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three point six is three ones and six tenths. The point marks the boundary between ones and tenths.

do.text: The point stays. The digits slide.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply by ten. Both digits slide one place left, together.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three tens and six ones. Thirty-six. Every digit is worth ten times as much.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: The point stayed put!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Multiply by ten again. The three becomes hundreds; the six becomes tens.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The empty ones place needs a zero. That is why multiplying a whole number by ten looks like adding a zero.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: But what matters is that every digit changes place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Two multiplications by ten make a hundred. We write ten squared, with a small raised two called an exponent.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten to the third power uses three factors of ten. Ten times ten times ten is one thousand.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Dividing reverses the motion. Each step right makes every digit worth one tenth as much.

do.text: Each step right: one tenth as much.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Divide three hundred sixty by one thousand. That is three steps right. First, thirty-six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Second, three point six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Third, zero point three six. A zero holds the empty ones place.
Three tenths and six hundredths: thirty-six hundredths.
beats.speaker: teacher
teacher
beats.say: What is sixteen point six three divided by ten to the first power? Think about the direction and the number of steps.

do.text: Choose the value and the reason

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: One step right. Each digit is worth one tenth as much.

do.text: Every digit becomes one tenth as much.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One point six six three. Keep the digits in the same order.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Watch the zeros in seven hundred ten and five hundred twenty. Divide both numbers by a hundred.

do.text: Zeros can hold places or add nothing

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One step right, then another.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven point one zero is seven point one. Five point two zero is five point two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Those zeros say zero hundredths. Leaving them off changes no value, and moves no other digit.

do.text: Trailing decimal zeros add no value.

beats.say: But some zeros must stay. Divide nine by a hundred.
beats.speaker: teacher

do.text: Keep zeros that hold a place

beats.say: One step right. Two steps right. The nine is in the hundredths place.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Zero ones, zero tenths, nine hundredths. Zero point zero nine.
beats.speaker: teacher

beats.say: Leave out that zero in the tenths place, and you get nine tenths. A different number.
beats.speaker: teacher
teacher
beats.say: Zero point one means one tenth. Multiplying by one tenth takes one of ten equal shares.

do.text: Multiplying by a tenth takes a tenth
Take one of ten equal shares.

beats.say: It is the same as dividing by ten.
beats.speaker: teacher
teacher
beats.say: Seventy-six point two becomes seven point six two. Every digit steps right once.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: And multiplying by zero point zero one takes a hundredth, so that is two steps right?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Yes. Start from seventy-six point two again.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One step to the right. A second step to the right. Zero point seven six two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: But dividing by a tenth asks a different question: how many tenths fit in four wholes?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each whole holds ten tenths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Ten here. Twenty altogether. Thirty. Forty.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Four wholes contain forty tenths. The answer counts the little pieces!

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: That is why dividing by a tenth multiplies the number by ten.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: On the chart, four divided by a tenth sends the four one place left, to four tens.

do.text: Dividing by a tenth: one step left

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Forty. A positive number divided by a tenth gets bigger, because we are counting smaller pieces.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A hundredth is smaller again. Ten rows of ten equal pieces make a hundred hundredths in one whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Each little piece is zero point zero one. Counting hundredths gives a hundred pieces for every whole.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So dividing by a hundredth is multiplying by a hundred. Two steps left.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try seventy-four point seven divided by zero point zero one.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One step to the left. A second step to the left. Fill the ones place with zero.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Seven thousand four hundred seventy hundredths fit in seventy-four point seven.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A factor is a number being multiplied. This factor is missing.
What number times one hundredth equals zero point four one two?
beats.speaker: teacher
learner
beats.say: Multiplying by a hundredth moves right twice. To find where we started, I reverse it. One step left. A second step left.

do.text: Undo two steps right with two steps left.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Forty-one point two. Check by going back: one step right, then another. We get zero point four one two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The missing factor is forty-one point two.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The same idea compares two matching digits. In three hundred twenty-one thousand, eight hundred fifty-eight, compare the two eights.

do.text: Close view: the last three places.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The left eight is in the hundreds place, worth eight hundred. The right eight is in the ones place, worth eight.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: From ones to tens: one step. From tens to hundreds: two steps.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Only one digit is between the eights, but there are two steps between their places.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: So the eight in the hundreds place is worth a hundred times as much as the eight in the ones place.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For three steps, multiply three tens: a thousand. For four steps, four tens: ten thousand. Count the steps, wherever the matching digits are.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Three point six. Multiply by ten: thirty-six.

do.text: The point stays. The digits slide.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Divide by ten, and we are back to three point six.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Left makes each digit worth ten times as much. Right makes it worth one tenth as much.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The point stays. The digits slide. Each step is a factor of ten.
